extracted.intended_audience: grant reviewers, funding program officers, and collaborators evaluating a biomedical/biophysical research proposal
extracted.subtask_description: A research strategy section of a biomedical/biophysical grant proposal describing aims, specific experimental methods (fluorescence, ITC, stopped-flow, NMR, X-ray, modeling), controls, replication, expected outcomes, alternatives, mentoring and timeline for a 3-year project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replication and technical replicates
rubrics_metrics.description: All experiments will be performed in triplicates; averages of at least three titrations and use of at least two different protein preparations will be used as controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stopped-flow: record 1000 pairs of data per experiment and average sets of data from 5–7 shots to improve signal-to-noise. Use replicates to compute means and standard deviations; replicate strategy applied across fluorescence, ITC, stopped-flow, HPLC, depurination, aniline cleavage, luminescent assays and cell-based cytotoxicity assays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Data will be subjected to statistical analysis; compute mean and standard deviation (σ) and report quantitative parameters with measures of variability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify most perturbed residues as those whose shift changes are greater than σ. Fit data by minimizing sum of squared errors using GraphPad Prism Solver or appropriate software; report standard deviations for thermodynamic/kinetic parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of appropriate positive and negative controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Include positive and negative controls in all assays (e.g., eukaryotic 28S rRNA as positive control for depurination, poly(C) as negative control; assay samples lacking VPg as positive control for depurination; RTA-lacking samples as negative control; catalytically inactive RTA as binding control; different His-tagged protein as negative control in cytotoxicity assays).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simultaneous measurements of individual protein spectra and all buffer solutions as controls for fluorescence. Use internal standards (e.g., N6-ethenoadenine) and standard curves for HPLC quantification. Confirm aniline treatment controls to rule out RNase contamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complementary and orthogonal methodological approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine multiple complementary techniques (direct fluorescence titrations, ITC, stopped-flow anisotropy, NMR, X-ray crystallography, molecular modeling/docking, site-directed mutagenesis, cell cytotoxicity assays) to characterize binding thermodynamics, kinetics, structure, and function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use orthogonal methods to confirm findings (e.g., ITC to confirm fluorescence-derived thermodynamics; NMR/X-ray to map interfaces; modeling to predict mutations; functional assays to correlate binding with inhibition). Describe alternatives when a technique fails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defined data-fitting models and analysis pipelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify models and equations for analyzing data (single- and double-exponential fits for anisotropy; ΔF = Fc – Fs for fluorescence; inner-filter correction Fcorr = Fobs · antilog[(Aex + Aem)/2]; adjusted chemical shift Δδ = sqrt[(ΔδH)^2 + (0.2·ΔδN)^2]; hyperbolic isotherm for chemical shift titrations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform nonlinear fitting using Global analysis software (OLIS) for stopped-flow and GraphPad Prism Solver for fluorescence/NMR fits; minimize sum of squared errors; report fitted parameters (kobs, kobs1/kobs2, Δr, Δr1/Δr2, Kd, ΔH, ΔS, ΔG).

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrumentation and experimental conditions specified
rubrics_metrics.description: Use appropriate, specified instrumentation and conditions (e.g., OLIS RSM 1000 stopped-flow with 1-ms dead time, Bruker Avance 600 MHz NMR at 298 K with three-channel TXI-cryoprobe, Nano ITC (TA Instruments), Waters HPLC with specified detectors and column).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain controlled temperatures (e.g., 25 °C for stopped-flow), use Shigemi microtubes for NMR, specify excitation/emission wavelengths for intrinsic and extrinsic fluorescence, employ reference photomultiplier and temperature-controlled circulating bath for stopped-flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for declaring binding or lack thereof
rubrics_metrics.description: Define observable behaviors that indicate binding: saturation binding behavior in titrations and fluorescence changes; decrease in adenines released from depurinated substrate RNA correlates with inhibition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VPg mutants that do not bind RTA will not show saturation binding nor decreased adenine release; compare fluorescence-derived Kd to NMR residue-specific apparent Kd values to corroborate binding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance threshold for NMR chemical shift perturbations
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate adjusted chemical shift Δδ and identify the most perturbed residues as those whose shift changes are greater than the mean standard deviation σ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fit chemical shift perturbation data for each perturbed residue to an isotherm to derive apparent Kd; compare residue-specific Kd to overall Kd from Aim 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of extrinsic labeling and controls for perturbation
rubrics_metrics.description: When using extrinsic fluorophores (e.g., NHS-fluorescein), label limited sites (one or two amines), confirm labeled site by digestion and HPLC, and perform controls to verify the probe has not perturbed equilibrium (label each protein separately and titrate with the unlabeled partner).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform simultaneous measurements of individual protein spectra and buffer solutions; use catalytically inactive RTA as additional control to assess labeling effects on binding and function.

rubrics_metrics.name: HPLC assay quantification and internal standard use
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantify adenine released from rRNA by HPLC using retention time and internal standard (N6-ethenoadenine) and analyze peak areas with Empower chromatography software.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reverse-phase XBridge C18 column with ammonium acetate/methanol elution, specified detector wavelengths (absorbance 254 nm, fluorescence λex=315 nm/λem=415 nm), construct standard curve and statistically analyze data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative/backup assays and contingency planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe alternative assays and fallback plans (e.g., aniline cleavage assay, luminescent coupled assay for adenine, use HCT-8 cells if Vero assays not suitable, send samples to external crystallization services or core facilities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state alternatives for each aim and when they will be used; leverage collaborators and external facilities for specialized techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crystallography screening strategy and occupancy considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use commercial crystallization screens (Hampton Research index/crystal/detergent screens sampling up to 230 conditions), soak RTA crystals with 2–3-fold excess VPg and vary conditions to improve ligand occupancy and electron density.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect X-ray diffraction at beamlines (e.g., X29A), process data with HKL2000, compare multiple crystals for consistency; send to specialist centers (e.g., Hauptman-Woodward) if crystals are not diffracting well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Molecular modeling/docking workflow and scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ bioinformatics tools to map interactions using docking and scoring algorithms (FlexX, GOLD, AutoDock, DOCK), keep n best poses, apply affinity scoring functions to rank poses, and consider protein flexibility and threading/homology modeling when required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain small molecule structure data from sources like DrugBank when applicable; explore algorithms that track previously discovered minima to sample large search spaces; use predicted models to guide site-directed mutagenesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site-directed mutagenesis methodology and positive control
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Stratagene’s QuickChange Site-Directed Mutagenesis Kit for efficient (>80%) site-specific mutations in double-stranded plasmids; include positive control reaction (pWhitescript 4.5-kb plasmid).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eliminate need for M13-based subcloning; generate mutants for point mutations, amino-acid switching, deletions/insertions and then express and purify constructs for functional and binding studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional correlation of binding to inhibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Correlate quantitative binding measurements (Kd, thermodynamics, kinetics) with functional assays of RTA activity (depurination, cytotoxicity) to establish that binding leads to inhibition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multiple functional readouts (HPLC adenine release, primer extension, aniline cleavage, luminescent assay, cell cytotoxicity CD50) and perform statistical comparisons across conditions with/without VPg constructs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cell-based cytotoxicity assay design and controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform Vero cell cytotoxicity assays in 96-well plates to test toxin inhibition by VPg, fix and stain cells, and measure absorbance at 630 nm; determine CD50 and specific toxin activity with appropriate controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use alternative cell line HCT-8 if needed; define CD50 as reciprocal of toxin dilution causing 50% cell loss relative to control, and calculate specific toxin activity as CD50/mL divided by toxin concentration in mg/mL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training, mentoring, and student involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrate undergraduate (and graduate) students into the research via the PRISM program and an Undergraduate Research Internship course (FOS 402); pair senior students with incoming students and provide hands-on mentorship and incremental responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide training in literature searches, project design, sampling, data analysis, and scientific communication; offer stipends, travel grants, GRE prep, and career advising to support student development and diversity in STEM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline, milestones, and dissemination expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Present a tentative 3-year timeline with Year 1 focusing on purification and thermodynamics (fluorescence/ITC), Year 2 on kinetics and depurination/crystallography, and Year 3 on extrinsic labeling, modeling, and mutagenesis; expect at least one publication per funded year and conference presentations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the timeline to structure milestones and collaborator visits; track progress against aims and prepare outputs for publications and meetings (American Plant Biology Society, Biophysical Society).
